# districtry

> Click a point, or type an address, and see every civic district that covers it — and who holds those seats. 14 instances across Illinois, New York, San Francisco, Wisconsin, Iowa, Michigan, Minnesota, Kentucky, Indiana, North Carolina, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee and Arkansas. Every boundary and every name comes from a published source and is cited to it.

Free, no account, no tracking of individuals. The map runs in the browser; what each page sends to whom is listed at https://districtry.com/privacy.html.

## The whole site

- [districtry](https://districtry.com/): the front door. Type an address and it opens whichever instance covers it, with the point already selected; a point nobody covers is told so rather than routed somewhere wrong.
- [Privacy](https://districtry.com/privacy.html)
- [Sponsorship](https://districtry.com/sponsorship.html)
- [Traffic report](https://districtry.com/traffic.html)
- [About districtry](https://districtry.com/about.html)
- [How districtry uses AI](https://districtry.com/ai.html)
- [Report a problem or leave a comment](https://districtry.com/feedback.html)

## Illinois

94 counties. Wards, county boards, police districts and beats, school zones, judicial subcircuits, and the people who hold those seats.

- [Illinois district lookup](https://districtry.com/il/): 41 layers, 94 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/il/congress.html)
- [Who is my county commissioner?](https://districtry.com/il/county-board.html): links a page per county, 97 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Who runs my fire protection district?](https://districtry.com/il/fire-district.html)
- [What judicial subcircuit am I in?](https://districtry.com/il/judicial-subcircuit.html)
- [Who runs my library district?](https://districtry.com/il/library-district.html)
- [Who runs my park district?](https://districtry.com/il/park-district.html)
- [What Chicago police district am I in?](https://districtry.com/il/police-district.html)
- [Which counties publish precinct maps?](https://districtry.com/il/precinct-maps.html)
- [What voting precinct am I in? Illinois](https://districtry.com/il/precinct.html)
- [Which CPS school board district am I in?](https://districtry.com/il/school-board.html)
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/il/sources.html)
- [Who is my Illinois state legislator?](https://districtry.com/il/state-legislature.html)
- [Who is my Supreme Court justice?](https://districtry.com/il/supreme-court.html)
- [What township am I in?](https://districtry.com/il/township.html)
- [Who is my alderman? Chicago wards](https://districtry.com/il/ward.html)
- [Chicago district questions](https://districtry.com/il/faq.html)
- [History](https://districtry.com/il/history.html)

## Michigan

All 83 counties: commissioner districts, compiled by the state from the plan each county's apportionment commission files — plus townships and charter townships, cities and villages, school districts and intermediate school districts, circuit courts and Court of Appeals districts, and the Michigan Senate, House and U.S. House seats, and who holds those.

- [Michigan district lookup](https://districtry.com/mi/): 19 layers, all 83 counties.
- [Who is on my city council?](https://districtry.com/mi/city-council.html)
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/mi/congress.html)
- [County commissioner district lookup](https://districtry.com/mi/county-commissioner.html): links a page per county, 83 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/mi/sources.html)
- [Who is my Michigan legislator?](https://districtry.com/mi/state-legislature.html)
- [Michigan district questions](https://districtry.com/mi/faq.html)
- [History](https://districtry.com/mi/history.html)

## Minnesota

All 87 counties and their county commissioner districts: judicial and watershed districts, townships and cities, voting precincts, school districts and school board districts, ZIP codes, tribal land, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the Minnesota Senate, House and U.S. House districts, and who holds the U.S. House seats. County commissioners, school board members and the councils of the cities over 25,000 people are named for the winner of each seat's most recent election in the Secretary of State's results, and a tribal council is named where the nation publishes its own list. Nobody is named yet on the judges' benches, the two state chambers or the smaller cities' councils, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [Minnesota district lookup](https://districtry.com/mn/): 19 layers, all 87 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/mn/congress.html)
- [County commissioner district lookup](https://districtry.com/mn/county-commissioner.html): links a page per county, 87 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/mn/sources.html)

## Kentucky

All 120 counties: each county's fiscal court and elected officers, cities with their mayors and councils, school districts, and the Supreme Court, Court of Appeals, circuit court and district court districts — plus the Kentucky Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with the member named for each U.S. House seat. County and city officials are named from the Department for Local Government's directories, and judges from the Court of Justice's own pages. Nobody is named yet on the two state chambers or the school boards, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [Kentucky district lookup](https://districtry.com/ky/): 12 layers, all 120 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/ky/congress.html)
- [Who runs my county?](https://districtry.com/ky/county-government.html): links a page per county, 120 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/ky/sources.html)
- [Kentucky district questions](https://districtry.com/ky/faq.html)

## Indiana

All 92 counties: each county's commissioners and county council, townships, cities and towns, school districts, ZIP codes, the Pokagon Band's trust land, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the Indiana Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with the member named for each U.S. House seat. County officials, and the mayors and councils of most places over 25,000 people, are named for the winner of each seat's most recent election in the Election Division's certified results; the Pokagon Band's council is named from its own page. Nobody is named yet on the two state chambers, the school boards, the township boards or the smaller towns' councils, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [Indiana district lookup](https://districtry.com/in/): 12 layers, all 92 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/in/congress.html)
- [Who are my county commissioners?](https://districtry.com/in/county-commissioner.html): links a page per county, 92 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/in/sources.html)
- [Indiana district questions](https://districtry.com/in/faq.html)

## North Carolina

All 100 counties: each county's board of commissioners, townships, cities and towns, school districts, ZIP codes, the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians' land, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the North Carolina Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with the member named for every seat. County commissioners are named for the winner of each seat's most recent election in the State Board of Elections' results. Nobody is named yet on the city councils, the school boards or the Eastern Band's council, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [North Carolina district lookup](https://districtry.com/nc/): 12 layers, all 100 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/nc/congress.html)
- [Who are my county commissioners?](https://districtry.com/nc/county-commissioner.html): links a page per county, 99 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/nc/sources.html)
- [Who is my NC legislator?](https://districtry.com/nc/state-legislature.html)
- [District questions](https://districtry.com/nc/faq.html)

## Oklahoma

All 77 counties and their commissioner districts: cities and towns, school districts, ZIP codes, the tribal areas the Census draws, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the Oklahoma Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with a member named for every U.S. House seat and nearly every legislative one. Each county's three commissioners are named from the State Election Board's roster. Nobody is named yet on the city councils, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [Oklahoma district lookup](https://districtry.com/ok/): 13 layers, all 77 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/ok/congress.html)
- [County commissioner district lookup](https://districtry.com/ok/county-commissioner.html): links a page per county, 77 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/ok/sources.html)
- [Who is my Oklahoma legislator?](https://districtry.com/ok/state-legislature.html)
- [District questions](https://districtry.com/ok/faq.html)

## South Carolina

All 46 counties and their county council districts: cities and towns, school districts, ZIP codes, the Catawba Nation's land, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the South Carolina Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with the member named for every seat. Each council seat names the winner of its most recent election in the State Election Commission's certified results. Nobody is named yet on the city councils or school boards, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [South Carolina district lookup](https://districtry.com/sc/): 12 layers, all 46 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/sc/congress.html)
- [Who is on my county council?](https://districtry.com/sc/county-council.html): links a page per county, 46 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.

## Tennessee

All 95 counties and their county commission districts: cities and towns, school districts, ZIP codes, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the Tennessee Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with who holds each seat. County commissioners are named from each county's own pages where the county publishes a current list, and the Data gaps panel lists the counties not named yet and why.

- [Tennessee district lookup](https://districtry.com/tn/): 13 layers, all 95 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/tn/congress.html)
- [County commission district lookup](https://districtry.com/tn/county-commissioner.html): links a page per county, 56 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/tn/sources.html)
- [Who is my Tennessee legislator?](https://districtry.com/tn/state-legislature.html)
- [Tennessee district questions](https://districtry.com/tn/faq.html)

## Arkansas

All 75 counties and their quorum court districts: cities and towns, school districts, ZIP codes, and the nearest police station, fire station and post office — plus the Arkansas Senate, House and U.S. House districts, with who holds each seat. Every county judge is named, and so is the justice of the peace for nearly every district, from the county's own site where it numbers its justices and otherwise from the 2024 election results while the winner is still on the Association of Arkansas Counties' list. Nobody is named yet on the city councils or school boards, and the Data gaps panel says why.

- [Arkansas district lookup](https://districtry.com/ar/): 11 layers, all 75 counties.
- [Who is my U.S. representative?](https://districtry.com/ar/congress.html)
- [Who is on my quorum court?](https://districtry.com/ar/quorum-court.html): links a page per county, 75 of them, each naming every member with whatever contact details that county publishes.
- [Sources & data layers](https://districtry.com/ar/sources.html)
- [Who is my Arkansas legislator?](https://districtry.com/ar/state-legislature.html)
- [Arkansas district questions](https://districtry.com/ar/faq.html)

## Where the answers come from

Each instance's sources page carries one row per layer: what it answers, the publisher its boundary comes from, where the names on its card come from, and the ground it answers on. That page is generated from the same list that registers the layers, so a layer cannot ship without a row.

Officeholder names are never guessed. Where no verifiable roster exists, a card links the official body instead of inventing a name, and what the project does not know is recorded rather than left blank — each instance ships a machine-readable list of its own gaps at `<instance>/data/app/coverage-gaps.json`.

Sources last reverified between October 10, 2026 and September 29, 2026, per instance.

This is a civic reference tool and it disclaims legal precision. Confirm a district assignment with the government office that draws it before relying on it for anything official.

## Terms

`https://districtry.com/robots.txt` publishes a Content-Signal, and these are the values in it: ai-input=yes, ai-train=no, search=yes, use=reference.

In plain words: indexing and search are welcome, and so is grounding an answer in these pages, on the terms the signal names — by reference, with a link back to the page that names the person, so a reader can check the government source behind it. Training is reserved. No crawler is disallowed by name: a site that wants its answers found does not gain anything by refusing the clients that find them.

The boundaries and rosters are public records from the publishers each sources page names; this project's own work is the collection, the citation and the code.

Corrections: corrections@overberg.co. Source: https://github.com/ThursdaysFamous/districtry
